Hors Saison - Long Point for Picnic tables are stacked at the end of the season on the beach at Long Point, on the north shore of Lake Erie. Long Point, a sand spit and marsh, designated as a World Biosphere Reserve, is one of the largest bird and waterfowl migration and staging areas in North America.

Pictured Rocks Panorama Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore on the south shore of Lake Superior is certainly worth the time and money to visit. We only had a short time so we took the boat out of Munising, Michigan for their "3 Hour Tour". The shoreline is absolutely beautiful with all of the different rock formations, arches, towers, caves, and beaches.

The Grand Portal Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore is a 42 mile stretch on the south shore of Lake Superior in Munising Michigan. The Grand Portal is one of many geological features that you will see on your tour. Other ways to see the lakeshore is either by hiking the bluffs or kayaking parts of the shoreline. Imagine an early morning scene over Lake Superior in Minnesota. The horizon is just beginning to lighten with the dawn's first blush, casting faint hues of purple and gold onto the tranquil surface of the lake. The sky above is painted with streaks of oranges, yellows and reds, perfectly reflecting on the calm water surface. The surrounding environment is still enveloped in the quiet hush of early morning - the treeline on the far shore is silhouetted against the increasing light, and the occasional bird call echoes across the water.

"North Shore, Lake Superior," Franklin Carmichael, 1927. Canadian Franklin Carmichael (1890-1945) was one of the famous Group of Seven artists, who lovingly depicted the Canadian landscape, believed that direct contact with nature was vital to art, expressing spiritual values through art, and promoted an idea of a national Canadian artistic identity. Carmichael also worked as an illustrator, graphic artist, and teacher. Although his work was sometimes dismissed in his day, and he was considered perhaps the least of the Group of Seven, he's still well regarded today. From the Art Gallery of Ontario, Toronto.
